newsitem.title: USA: Southwestern Public div depends on merger.
newsitem.headline: Southwestern Public div depends on merger.

text.p: Southwestern Public Service Co said Wednesday its dividend payments depend on the timing of the Securities and Exchange Commission's approval of its pending merger with Public Service Co of Colorado.
Southwestern said it will pay an unchanged quarterly dividend of $0.55 a share on September 1, record August 15, if the merger, which will create New Century Energies, has not closed by August 15.

If the merger occurs before that date, the utility said it will pay a prorated dividend of $0.00597826 per day for the number of days elapsed since May 15 through the day preceding the date the merger becomes effective. The dividend will be payable on the first business day of the month after the effective date of the merger, to holders of record on the day before the effective date of the merger.

If the merger closes after August 15 but on or before November 1, Southwestern said it will pay a prorated dividend of $0.00597826 per day for the number of days elapsed since August 15 through the day preceding the date the merger becomes effective.
Finally, Southwestern said if the merger has not closed on or before November 1, it will not pay the prorated dividend for the period beginning August 16 and ending October 31.
Southwestern said it anticipates the newly-formed entity New Century Energies initially will pay dividends on its common stock of $2.32 annually.
